title: Per-account storage quota for file uploads
name: Upload quota tracker

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code enforces the per-account storage limit when many uploads for the same account arrive at once? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
If store.write throws an IOException in upload(), what is the state of the account's quota afterwards?
choices: The reserved bytes stay counted until the account's next successful upload corrects the total.
The reserved bytes are returned through release(), and the exception propagates to the caller.
The reserved bytes are returned and the exception is swallowed so the caller sees a failed UploadResult.
Nothing was reserved yet, because reservation happens only after the write succeeds.

questions.prompt: release() uses updateAndGet(current -> Math.max(0L, current - bytes)) rather than reading the value and calling set(). What does that buy?
choices: It makes release() block until no reservation for that account is in progress.
It guarantees the counter can never exceed limitBytes.
It retries the computation if another thread changed the counter in the meantime, so concurrent releases and reservations are not overwritten.
It avoids the cost of computeIfAbsent on the map.

questions.prompt: Two threads upload different files at the same path for the same account at the same moment. What does nextVersion() guarantee?
choices: Both uploads receive the same version, and the later write overwrites the earlier blob.
One of the two uploads fails because the merge call detects the conflict.
Both uploads receive the same version number only if their lengths match.
The two uploads receive different version numbers, so their blobs are stored under different keys.
